curriculum: NaCCA Religious and Moral Education Curriculum for Primary Schools (Basic 1–6), September 2019
question_format: Each indicator contains 20 questions. Multiple-choice answers use zero-based option indexes. Open responses use teacher-assessed criteria.

indicators.statement: Describe the nature of God through His attributes.

questions.prompt: Which attribute describes treating others with affection and care?
questions.hint: Think of affection shown through care.
questions.explanation: Love is shown through active care for another person.

questions.prompt: Name one attribute of God taught in the curriculum.
questions.hint: Think of a quality the lesson associates with God.
questions.explanation: Love, patience, mercy or all-knowing

questions.prompt: What does omniscient mean?
questions.hint: Look for the part of the word that concerns knowledge.
questions.explanation: The curriculum describes God as omniscient, meaning knowing all things.

questions.prompt: Explain patience in your own words.
questions.hint: Think about waiting for a turn without losing your temper.
questions.explanation: Remaining calm and enduring without giving up or harming others

criteria.description: Remaining calm and enduring without giving up or harming others

questions.prompt: A person forgives after an apology. Which attribute is shown?
questions.hint: Focus on how the mistake is treated after the apology.
questions.explanation: Mercy

questions.prompt: Match: love; patience; mercy with caring; waiting calmly; forgiving.
questions.hint: Decide which description belongs to each quality.
questions.explanation: love-caring, patience-waiting calmly, mercy-forgiving

criteria.description: love-caring, patience-waiting calmly, mercy-forgiving

questions.prompt: Which action reflects kindness?
questions.hint: Think about what the other person needs.
questions.explanation: Kindness gives practical help while respecting the person's needs.

questions.prompt: Give one way a learner can show patience at school.
questions.hint: Choose one moment when waiting helps a classmate.
questions.explanation: Wait a turn, listen calmly or keep trying

criteria.description: Wait a turn, listen calmly or keep trying

questions.prompt: Why should attributes such as love and mercy be practised?
questions.hint: Consider how the other person might feel afterward.
questions.explanation: They support good relationships and peaceful living

criteria.description: They support good relationships and peaceful living

questions.prompt: Draw an action that shows kindness.
questions.hint: Make the helpful action visible in your picture.
questions.explanation: A clear action showing safe care or help

criteria.description: A clear action showing safe care or help

questions.prompt: Which is not a positive attribute?
questions.hint: Consider how each quality affects someone else.
questions.explanation: Cruelty causes hurt. The other qualities support caring relationships.

questions.prompt: How can a person show honesty?
questions.hint: Think about what someone could observe.
questions.explanation: Speak truthfully and correct mistakes

criteria.description: Speak truthfully and correct mistakes

questions.prompt: State one difference between knowing an attribute and practising it.
questions.hint: Compare saying what kindness means with actually helping.
questions.explanation: Knowing is understanding it; practising is showing it in actions

criteria.description: Knowing is understanding it; practising is showing it in actions

questions.prompt: A learner shares fairly with a classmate. What attribute is shown?
questions.hint: Think about who benefits when something is shared.
questions.explanation: Love or generosity

criteria.description: Love or generosity

questions.prompt: Why should people avoid claiming to know everything?
questions.hint: Compare human learning with the meaning of omniscience.
questions.explanation: People need to learn and can make mistakes; the curriculum describes God as all-knowing.
options: A good guess is always correct

questions.prompt: Role-play a calm response to a disagreement.
questions.hint: Choose a disagreement both actors can safely discuss.
questions.explanation: Shows patience, respectful speech and listening

criteria.description: Shows patience, respectful speech and listening

questions.prompt: Name one way mercy can be shown after a mistake.
questions.hint: Think about both forgiveness and putting the mistake right.
questions.explanation: Forgive while guiding repair or improvement

criteria.description: Forgive while guiding repair or improvement

questions.prompt: Which behaviour best shows self-control?
questions.hint: Look for the choice that allows time to think.
questions.explanation: A pause gives the speaker time to choose calm words.

questions.prompt: Give one attribute and a safe daily example of it.
questions.hint: Start with a quality, then show it in a concrete action.
questions.explanation: For example, patience is shown when a learner waits quietly until a classmate has finished speaking. Name a quality and describe an action that demonstrates it.

criteria.description: For example, patience is shown when a learner waits quietly until a classmate has finished speaking. Name a quality and describe an action that demonstrates it.

questions.prompt: What is one benefit of practising positive attributes?
questions.hint: Describe what changes between the people involved.
questions.explanation: It builds trust, care and peace

criteria.description: It builds trust, care and peace

Apply the lesson to a situation and justify a choice.

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 foundational, 7 simple-use, 5 application and 3 challenge questions.

indicators.statement: Explain how humankind and the environment interrelate.

questions.prompt: Which living things release oxygen as they make food in sunlight?
questions.hint: Think about living things that release oxygen.
questions.explanation: Green plants release oxygen during photosynthesis. People and animals use oxygen to breathe.

questions.prompt: Name one thing people obtain from plants.
questions.hint: Think of something people use that comes from leaves, fruit or wood.
questions.explanation: Food, oxygen, medicine or shelter

questions.prompt: How do people depend on water?
questions.hint: Consider needs on a farm and at home.
questions.explanation: People depend on water to drink, grow crops and stay clean.
options: Only as a route for boats
For drinking, hygiene, farming and life

questions.prompt: What may happen when trees are cut without replacement?
questions.hint: Consider what lived on or under the trees.
questions.explanation: Loss of habitats, soil damage and less clean air

criteria.description: Loss of habitats, soil damage and less clean air

questions.prompt: Match each resource to its use: water, soil, trees. Choose from growing crops, drinking, and providing shade under a canopy.
questions.hint: Match each resource to something it makes possible.
questions.explanation: People drink clean water, grow crops in soil and find shade under the canopy of trees.

criteria.description: People drink clean water, grow crops in soil and find shade under the canopy of trees.

questions.prompt: How can people help plants survive?
questions.hint: What does a plant need after a seedling is planted?
questions.explanation: Plant and care for them; avoid destruction

criteria.description: Plant and care for them; avoid destruction

questions.prompt: What is an example of animals depending on plants?
questions.hint: Look for the direction of the benefit: what does the animal receive?
questions.explanation: Leaves provide food and branches provide shelter for some animals.
options: Using plants for food or shelter

questions.prompt: Explain one way people and animals depend on each other.
questions.hint: Follow the connection from the animal to the person or back again.
questions.explanation: A family may care for poultry by providing shelter and feed. The chickens may provide eggs for the family.

criteria.description: A family may care for poultry by providing shelter and feed. The chickens may provide eggs for the family.

questions.prompt: Why should refuse not be dumped in a river?
questions.hint: Follow the water downstream.
questions.explanation: It pollutes water and harms people and animals

criteria.description: It pollutes water and harms people and animals

questions.prompt: Draw a simple food or resource link in the environment.
questions.hint: Use an arrow to show who receives what.
questions.explanation: Shows a correct connection, such as plant-person-food

criteria.description: Shows a correct connection, such as plant-person-food

questions.prompt: Which action supports the environment?
questions.hint: Think about what keeps water usable downstream.
questions.explanation: Protecting a water source helps keep water available for the people and animals that use it.

questions.prompt: What does interrelationship mean?
questions.hint: Look for a connection running between living things.
questions.explanation: Things depending on or affecting one another

criteria.description: Things depending on or affecting one another

questions.prompt: A farmer plants trees near a damaged area. How can this help?
questions.hint: Think about roots and places animals can live.
questions.explanation: It can protect soil and improve habitats

criteria.description: It can protect soil and improve habitats

questions.prompt: What can polluted air affect?
questions.hint: Consider which living things encounter air.
questions.explanation: Polluted air can affect people, animals and plants that are exposed to it.

questions.prompt: Name one way animals help plants.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to seeds after an animal eats fruit.
questions.explanation: Seed dispersal or pollination

questions.prompt: Explain to a friend why littering affects others.
questions.hint: Consider who meets the waste after the first person leaves.
questions.explanation: Links litter to pollution, health or harm

criteria.description: Links litter to pollution, health or harm

questions.prompt: Why are ecosystems important?
questions.hint: Think about connections among living things and their surroundings.
questions.explanation: An ecosystem links organisms and resources such as water and soil that support life.
options: They remove the need for water
They allow every species to live alone

questions.prompt: Give one responsible use of land.
questions.hint: Think about keeping the soil usable next season.
questions.explanation: Farm carefully, protect soil or avoid harmful mining

criteria.description: Farm carefully, protect soil or avoid harmful mining

questions.prompt: Describe one environmental problem and one connected effect on people.
questions.hint: Begin with a change in land, air or water.
questions.explanation: Rubbish may pollute a stream, leaving neighbours with less clean water for everyday use. Accept another explained connection.

criteria.description: Rubbish may pollute a stream, leaving neighbours with less clean water for everyday use. Accept another explained connection.

questions.prompt: Why should humans care for other creatures?
questions.hint: Think about what a creature needs in order to live.
questions.explanation: They have a role in the environment and depend on it

criteria.description: They have a role in the environment and depend on it

indicators.content_standard: Appreciate the uniqueness of humankind and their environments

indicators.statement: Explain the religious and moral lessons in preserving the environment.

questions.prompt: What does stewardship mean?
questions.hint: Think about the duty of a person entrusted with something.
questions.explanation: A steward is responsible for how resources are used and cared for.
options: Using resources as fast as possible
Responsible care of what is entrusted to us

questions.prompt: State one moral reason for preserving the environment.
questions.hint: Think about the living things that share a place.
questions.explanation: To protect life, health or future generations

criteria.description: To protect life, health or future generations

questions.prompt: Which action preserves the environment?
questions.hint: Consider where the waste ends up.
questions.explanation: Using an appropriate waste collection point helps prevent harm to water, land and living things.

questions.prompt: Why is indiscriminate bush burning harmful?
questions.hint: Consider what an uncontrolled fire can reach.
questions.explanation: It destroys plants, animals and soil

criteria.description: It destroys plants, animals and soil

questions.prompt: Name one safe way to protect a water body.
questions.hint: Trace what might enter the water from its banks.
questions.explanation: Do not dump waste; protect the banks

criteria.description: Do not dump waste; protect the banks

questions.prompt: Why should mining follow legal and safe methods?
questions.hint: Think about responsibilities to people near the site.
questions.explanation: Following safeguards helps protect workers, communities, water and land.
options: To reduce harm to people and land
To avoid planning for damaged sites
To remove every tree near a site

questions.prompt: Explain why future generations matter in environmental care.
questions.hint: Imagine a person using the same river many years later.
questions.explanation: They will also need healthy resources

criteria.description: They will also need healthy resources

questions.prompt: Match each action to the most direct benefit: planting trees, collecting litter, careful fishing. Choose from keeping a market clean, restoring tree cover, and protecting aquatic life.
questions.hint: Look at what changes in the soil, the surroundings and the water.
questions.explanation: Planting trees restores tree cover, collecting litter keeps a market clean, and careful fishing helps protect aquatic life.

criteria.description: Planting trees restores tree cover, collecting litter keeps a market clean, and careful fishing helps protect aquatic life.

questions.prompt: A community cleans a market area. What value is shown?
questions.hint: What duty have the people accepted?
questions.explanation: Responsibility or care

criteria.description: Responsibility or care

questions.prompt: Which is a moral lesson of conservation?
questions.hint: Consider creatures that depend on the same habitat.
questions.explanation: Caring for habitat respects the needs of other living things as well as those of people.
options: Use every resource before others can
Respect other creatures' right to survive
Keep only creatures with a selling price
Leave damaged habitats for others to fix

questions.prompt: Give one reason to avoid plastic litter.
questions.hint: Think about where the litter may travel when it rains.
questions.explanation: It can block drains and harm animals or water

criteria.description: It can block drains and harm animals or water

questions.prompt: Draw a poster idea encouraging environmental care.
questions.hint: Show an action a viewer could take.
questions.explanation: A poster might show litter going into a collection bin instead of a river. Its image and caption should make the protective action clear.

criteria.description: A poster might show litter going into a collection bin instead of a river. Its image and caption should make the protective action clear.

questions.prompt: What can afforestation help prevent?
questions.hint: Think about what new tree cover and roots do.
questions.explanation: Planting and caring for trees can restore cover and help hold soil in place.
options: Loss of trees and soil erosion

questions.prompt: How does preserving the environment promote health?
questions.hint: Link a healthy environment with something people use every day.
questions.explanation: It reduces pollution and supports clean air and water

criteria.description: It reduces pollution and supports clean air and water

questions.prompt: Someone suggests burning all the grass near nesting birds to tidy a shared space. What concern should the class raise?
questions.hint: Think about an action that could damage nearby living things.
questions.explanation: An uncontrolled fire can destroy nesting places. The class could suggest a supervised clean-up that protects living things.

criteria.description: An uncontrolled fire can destroy nesting places. The class could suggest a supervised clean-up that protects living things.

questions.prompt: Role-play a respectful campaign message about clean surroundings.
questions.hint: Give your audience one action they can carry out.
questions.explanation: Invite the class to place rubbish in the collection bins and explain how this keeps the courtyard clean for everyone. Accept another accurate and courteous invitation.

criteria.description: Invite the class to place rubbish in the collection bins and explain how this keeps the courtyard clean for everyone. Accept another accurate and courteous invitation.

questions.prompt: Which action is least responsible?
questions.hint: Follow where rubbish goes when rain carries it.
questions.explanation: Refuse can block a drain and pollute water used by others.

questions.prompt: Name one environmental duty at school.
questions.hint: Choose a task appropriate to a learner's age.
questions.explanation: Use bins, conserve water or join clean-up work

criteria.description: Use bins, conserve water or join clean-up work

questions.prompt: Plan one safe class environmental activity.
questions.hint: Decide what the group will do and who can supervise.
questions.explanation: Realistic activity with safety and responsibility

criteria.description: Realistic activity with safety and responsibility

questions.prompt: Why is environmental preservation a shared duty?
questions.hint: Think about both shared use and shared effects.
questions.explanation: Everyone uses and affects the environment

criteria.description: Everyone uses and affects the environment

indicators.statement: Discuss the importance of prayer in our lives.

questions.prompt: Prayer is best described as what?
questions.hint: Think about whom a worshipper addresses.
questions.explanation: In the traditions studied, prayer is a way for worshippers to communicate with the object of worship.
options: Communication between a worshipper and the object of worship

questions.prompt: Name one type of prayer.
questions.hint: Recall a purpose prayer can serve for a believer.
questions.explanation: Thanksgiving, confession, intercession or supplication

questions.prompt: Which prayer expresses gratitude?
questions.hint: A family wants to express appreciation after a harvest.
questions.explanation: A prayer of thanksgiving expresses gratitude. A petition asks for help.

questions.prompt: A person asks for help in a difficult time. What type of prayer is this?
questions.hint: Is the speaker expressing thanks or making a request?
questions.explanation: Supplication

questions.prompt: What is intercession?
questions.hint: Think about the person whose needs are mentioned.
questions.explanation: Praying on behalf of others

criteria.description: Praying on behalf of others

questions.prompt: Which name does the Islamic tradition use for the five daily obligatory prayers?
questions.hint: The question concerns the daily prayers named in Islam.
questions.explanation: Salat is the name used in the lesson for the five daily compulsory prayers in Islam.

questions.prompt: State one reason prayer is important to believers.
questions.hint: Consider the relationship to God described in the lesson.
questions.explanation: It may express dependence, gratitude, guidance or closeness to God

criteria.description: It may express dependence, gratitude, guidance or closeness to God

questions.prompt: Match thanksgiving, confession and supplication to these examples: asking for help, expressing thanks and admitting a wrong.
questions.hint: Look for gratitude, admission of a wrong and asking for help.
questions.explanation: Thanksgiving expresses thanks, confession acknowledges a wrong, and supplication asks for help.

criteria.description: Thanksgiving expresses thanks, confession acknowledges a wrong, and supplication asks for help.

questions.prompt: A class display puts the five daily Salat and congregational Friday prayer under the same heading. Explain how their descriptions differ.
questions.hint: Compare a daily obligation with a congregational gathering.
questions.explanation: Salat refers here to the five daily obligatory prayers. The lesson also identifies Jumu’ah as congregational Friday prayer.

criteria.description: Salat refers here to the five daily obligatory prayers. The lesson also identifies Jumu’ah as congregational Friday prayer.

questions.prompt: Which description fits a prayer of intercession?
questions.hint: Consider whose needs are being brought before God.
questions.explanation: Intercession involves praying on behalf of another person.

questions.prompt: Give one respectful behaviour near a place of prayer.
questions.hint: Think about giving other people space.
questions.explanation: Keep quiet, follow rules or avoid disturbance

criteria.description: Keep quiet, follow rules or avoid disturbance

questions.prompt: Draw a two-part chart showing thanksgiving and supplication. Label each with the purpose of the prayer.
questions.hint: Make the words describe the purpose of the prayer.
questions.explanation: Thanksgiving expresses gratitude. Supplication asks for help. Give a suitable caption or example for each.

criteria.description: Thanksgiving expresses gratitude. Supplication asks for help. Give a suitable caption or example for each.

questions.prompt: Which statement is fair?
questions.hint: Think about a shared purpose and different ways to express it.
questions.explanation: Traditions may share purposes such as gratitude while using different forms of prayer.
options: Prayer always uses the same words
Every prayer asks for an object
Prayer practices may differ among religions

questions.prompt: How can prayer encourage gratitude?
questions.hint: Think about why a worshipper would name something good they received.
questions.explanation: It gives believers a way to give thanks

criteria.description: It gives believers a way to give thanks

questions.prompt: A Christian worshipper and a Traditional worshipper each give thanks. What can a pupil conclude from these examples?
questions.hint: Use the Christian and Traditional examples given in the lesson.
questions.explanation: Thanksgiving is a purpose found in both examples. The examples do not establish that the forms of worship are identical.

criteria.description: Thanksgiving is a purpose found in both examples. The examples do not establish that the forms of worship are identical.

questions.prompt: Demonstrate respectful conduct while others have a quiet reflection time.
questions.hint: Explain what a visitor can notice without guessing anyone's beliefs.
questions.explanation: Shows calmness, privacy and respect

criteria.description: Shows calmness, privacy and respect

questions.prompt: Why might believers pray for others?
questions.hint: Whose wellbeing does the worshipper have in mind?
questions.explanation: Praying on behalf of others can express care for their wellbeing.
options: To list only their own achievements

questions.prompt: Name one way people can show the values they pray about.
questions.hint: Connect words about helping others with an action.
questions.explanation: Act kindly, honestly, peacefully or responsibly

criteria.description: Act kindly, honestly, peacefully or responsibly

questions.prompt: Explain one type of prayer and its purpose.
questions.hint: Give an example that helps distinguish the purpose of this prayer.
questions.explanation: For example, intercession means praying on behalf of others, such as asking for help for a neighbour in difficulty.

criteria.description: For example, intercession means praying on behalf of others, such as asking for help for a neighbour in difficulty.

questions.prompt: What is one moral benefit of respectful prayer practices?
questions.hint: Choose a value that can affect the next decision.
questions.explanation: They can encourage humility, gratitude or care

criteria.description: They can encourage humility, gratitude or care

indicators.statement: Gather and record data on religious festivals.

questions.prompt: Which is a religious festival celebrated in Ghana?
questions.hint: Look for a named celebration in the lesson's festival list.
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Fitr appears among the festivals celebrated in Ghana.

questions.prompt: Name one Christian festival.
questions.hint: Think about the lesson's Christian examples.
questions.explanation: Christmas or Easter

questions.prompt: Name one of the two Eid festivals in the curriculum list.
questions.hint: Recall the two Eid festivals named in the class list.
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Fitr or Eid-ul-Adha

criteria.description: eid al-fitr; eid ul-fitr; eid-ul-fitr; eid al-adha; eid ul-adha; eid-ul-adha

questions.prompt: The class list includes Damba and Tedudu. Choose one and name a source that could help you find out how it is celebrated.
questions.hint: Look for a named local celebration in a source.
questions.explanation: For example, ask a knowledgeable participant about Damba, or use a captioned class record of Tedudu.

criteria.description: For example, ask a knowledgeable participant about Damba, or use a captioned class record of Tedudu.

questions.prompt: What is a useful way to gather festival information?
questions.hint: Consider who can explain the celebration from experience.
questions.explanation: A knowledgeable community source can describe the activities and help the class check its notes.
options: Adding details to fill a blank

questions.prompt: Why should a learner record the source of festival information?
questions.hint: Imagine returning to check the detail a week later.
questions.explanation: To show where information came from and check accuracy

criteria.description: To show where information came from and check accuracy

questions.prompt: Read these interview notes: Amina says her family celebrates Eid-ul-Fitr; Kojo mentions Easter; Sena describes Tedudu. Match each speaker with the festival named.
questions.hint: Put each activity under the festival named by the speaker.
questions.explanation: Amina describes Eid-ul-Fitr, Kojo describes Easter and Sena describes Tedudu. Each match comes from the speaker’s own note.

criteria.description: Amina describes Eid-ul-Fitr, Kojo describes Easter and Sena describes Tedudu. Each match comes from the speaker’s own note.

questions.prompt: What detail could be recorded about a festival?
questions.hint: Think of a field in a festival notebook.
questions.explanation: Name, place, time, activities or purpose

criteria.description: Name, place, time, activities or purpose

questions.prompt: Which source is most reliable for a class project?
questions.hint: Check who supplied the information and how they know.
questions.explanation: A knowledgeable source can explain what was observed. Recording that source makes the account easier to check.
options: A caption copied without its source
A guess based on one costume
A teacher-approved source or knowledgeable community member
An anonymous message with no details

questions.prompt: Describe one respectful question to ask about a festival.
questions.hint: Choose a question about what people do during the celebration.
questions.explanation: What activities are important during the festival?

criteria.description: What activities are important during the festival?

questions.prompt: A source disagrees with another source. What should learners do?
questions.hint: Keep track of who gave each account.
questions.explanation: Record the difference and verify with reliable guidance

criteria.description: Record the difference and verify with reliable guidance

questions.prompt: Make a simple chart heading for festival data.
questions.hint: Use headings a reader can distinguish at a glance.
questions.explanation: Festival name, community, time, activities or meaning

criteria.description: Festival name, community, time, activities or meaning

questions.prompt: Why should festival data be gathered respectfully?
questions.hint: Think about whose practices the class is describing.
questions.explanation: Respect includes asking permission and representing people's accounts accurately.
options: It removes the need for permission
It allows private details to be published

questions.prompt: Name one non-personal source of festival information.
questions.hint: Think about something the class can view or read together.
questions.explanation: Book, poster, teacher material, museum or approved video

criteria.description: Book, poster, teacher material, museum or approved video

questions.prompt: Can a learner invent festival details to fill a table?
questions.hint: Consider how to mark a fact that still needs to be checked.
questions.explanation: No; use verified information

criteria.description: No; use verified information

questions.prompt: Practise a polite interview about a festival.
questions.hint: Explain the purpose of the interview before asking your question.
questions.explanation: Uses respectful questions and listening

criteria.description: Uses respectful questions and listening

questions.prompt: What does recording data help learners do?
questions.hint: Think what a dated or labelled record lets you check.
questions.explanation: Keeping notes preserves details and allows comparisons across the accounts.

questions.prompt: State one rule for interviewing an elder or guest.
questions.hint: Think about the guest's time and consent.
questions.explanation: Ask permission, listen and thank the person

criteria.description: Ask permission, listen and thank the person

questions.prompt: From a class account of one festival, record its name, one activity and where that information came from.
questions.hint: Choose three different fields for a single festival.
questions.explanation: Use separate labels for the festival, the activity actually described, and the source (for example, a named class interview).

criteria.description: Use separate labels for the festival, the activity actually described, and the source (for example, a named class interview).

questions.prompt: Why may festivals be celebrated differently in different places?
questions.hint: Consider how a community passes on its customs.
questions.explanation: Communities have different customs and histories

criteria.description: Communities have different customs and histories

indicators.statement: Explain the need for celebrating various festivals.

questions.prompt: One reason communities celebrate festivals is to promote what?
questions.hint: Think of what bringing neighbours together may build.
questions.explanation: Sharing preparation and celebrations can strengthen unity.

questions.prompt: Name one reason people celebrate a festival.
questions.hint: Consider what happens between neighbours during a celebration.
questions.explanation: Remembrance, gratitude, unity, reconciliation or teaching values

criteria.description: Remembrance, gratitude, unity, reconciliation or teaching values

questions.prompt: People share food during a festival. What value can this show?
questions.hint: Think about what the person giving food is doing for others.
questions.explanation: Generosity or togetherness

criteria.description: Generosity or togetherness

questions.prompt: Which action can strengthen community ties during a festival?
questions.hint: Think how neighbours can make a guest feel included.
questions.explanation: Cooperation and a respectful welcome help people build relationships.

questions.prompt: How can festivals support reconciliation?
questions.hint: What could people do after a disagreement?
questions.explanation: They can bring people together to forgive and rebuild relationships

criteria.description: They can bring people together to forgive and rebuild relationships

questions.prompt: Explain one way a festival preserves culture.
questions.hint: Think about what a younger person can learn by watching.
questions.explanation: It passes on customs, stories, music or history

criteria.description: It passes on customs, stories, music or history

questions.prompt: Why should festival celebrations be safe?
questions.hint: Consider people taking part in a busy gathering.
questions.explanation: Planning for safety helps participants and visitors celebrate without avoidable harm.
options: To make every festival look alike
Safety protects participants and the community

questions.prompt: A neighbour describes sharing food and visiting relatives during a festival. Explain one reason these activities might matter to that community.
questions.hint: Ask a question that helps you understand the activity's purpose.
questions.explanation: Making time for relatives and sharing food can strengthen relationships. Use the activities in the neighbour’s account as evidence.

criteria.description: Making time for relatives and sharing food can strengthen relationships. Use the activities in the neighbour’s account as evidence.

questions.prompt: What can a festival teach about sacrifice?
questions.hint: Think about what the helper gives up for others.
questions.explanation: Giving up something or working for a meaningful purpose

criteria.description: Giving up something or working for a meaningful purpose

questions.prompt: Match each festival purpose to its description: unity, gratitude, remembrance. Choose from recalling an event, bringing people together and showing appreciation.

criteria.description: People deserve choice, dignity and protection

questions.prompt: A learner cannot join a task because of a disability or duty. Can they still be committed?
questions.hint: Think of contributions besides physical work.
questions.explanation: Yes, through another suitable contribution

criteria.description: Yes, through another suitable contribution

questions.prompt: What does a committed member avoid?
questions.hint: Think about the effects on people who use the facility.
questions.explanation: Damage and neglect can leave a whole community without a useful resource.
options: Telling an adult about a dangerous fault

questions.prompt: Role-play a meeting proposing a solution to littering.
questions.hint: Give each speaker a chance to suggest a solution.
questions.explanation: Respectful ideas, listening and practical solution

criteria.description: Respectful ideas, listening and practical solution

questions.prompt: Name one way to include others in community work.
questions.hint: Match a role to what the person can do.
questions.explanation: Offer suitable roles and respect different abilities

criteria.description: Offer suitable roles and respect different abilities

questions.prompt: How does commitment support harmony?
questions.hint: Think about how people learn to trust neighbours working alongside them.
questions.explanation: Cooperation gives members practice in solving common problems together.
options: It removes the need to listen
It gives one person every decision

questions.prompt: Explain one community duty and one benefit.
questions.hint: Link the duty directly to an effect on other residents.
questions.explanation: Reporting damage to a shared water tap can help the community arrange repairs and reduce wasted water. Accept another duty with a directly linked benefit.

criteria.description: Reporting damage to a shared water tap can help the community arrange repairs and reduce wasted water. Accept another duty with a directly linked benefit.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to keep promises made to a group?
questions.hint: Consider how one person's action affects the plans of others.
questions.explanation: It supports trust and reliable cooperation

criteria.description: It supports trust and reliable cooperation

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 foundational, 7 simple-use, 5 application and 3 challenge questions.

indicators.statement: Identify the role of children in promoting harmony with other family members.

questions.prompt: Two cousins both want to use one storybook. Which suggestion from a child could promote harmony?
options: Say the louder cousin owns it
Promise both cousins the same turn
Agree on a time for each reader
questions.hint: Think about both children's needs.
questions.explanation: An agreed turn lets both cousins read and reduces the cause of the quarrel.

questions.prompt: Complete the word used in this lesson. Living peacefully and working well together is living in _____.
questions.hint: Think about how family members get along.
questions.explanation: Harmony describes peaceful, cooperative relationships.

questions.prompt: A grandparent is speaking and a cousin interrupts. Suggest a sentence a child could say respectfully.
questions.hint: Think about making room for each speaker.
questions.explanation: For example, “May we hear the rest of Grandma's idea first?” invites listening without insulting the cousin.

criteria.description: For example, “May we hear the rest of Grandma's idea first?” invites listening without insulting the cousin.

questions.prompt: Kweku put the cups in the wrong cupboard. What could he do to show humility?
questions.hint: Think about what happens after someone points out a mistake.
questions.explanation: He could acknowledge his mistake, listen to the correction and return the cups to the agreed place.

criteria.description: He could acknowledge his mistake, listen to the correction and return the cups to the agreed place.

questions.prompt: Which action shows respect during a family discussion?
options: Listening before giving a different view
Deciding a younger child has no ideas
Interrupting to finish an elder's sentence
Agreeing aloud while mocking the speaker later
questions.hint: Think about how the speaker is treated.
questions.explanation: Listening shows the speaker that their contribution matters, even when opinions differ.

questions.prompt: Make two cards for a family discussion. Put one duty of a child on the first card and one supporting duty of an adult on the second.
questions.hint: Choose a safe activity they could do together.
questions.explanation: A child might put away shared materials while an adult explains where each item belongs. The roles fit together.

criteria.description: A child might put away shared materials while an adult explains where each item belongs. The roles fit together.

questions.prompt: A younger child asks for help finding a school bag. Give two ways an older sibling could help without taking over.
questions.hint: Think about sharing the search.
questions.explanation: The sibling might ask where it was last seen and help search one area while the child checks another.

criteria.description: The sibling might ask where it was last seen and help search one area while the child checks another.

questions.prompt: A child has agreed to set out plates before dinner. Which action is most reliable?
options: Wait until the meal is over to mention the duty
Set them out on time or tell the family early if help is needed
Say it is finished before checking
questions.hint: What would the other family members need to know?
questions.explanation: Doing the task, or giving notice of a difficulty, helps the family plan together.

questions.prompt: Act out a short exchange between an aunt and a child who disagrees about where to keep shared books.
questions.hint: Give each person a chance to speak.
questions.explanation: The child can explain their reason calmly and listen to the aunt. The pair can agree on a place both can find.

criteria.description: The child can explain their reason calmly and listen to the aunt. The pair can agree on a place both can find.

questions.prompt: Draw two panels showing a family disagreement and a child's helpful response. Add a caption to each panel.
questions.hint: Show what the child actually does.
questions.explanation: One panel might show two relatives reaching for a radio. The next might show the child suggesting turns, with captions explaining the change.

criteria.description: One panel might show two relatives reaching for a radio. The next might show the child suggesting turns, with captions explaining the change.

questions.prompt: A learner says harmony means younger people can never raise a concern. Which response is fairest?
options: Children must pretend that nothing is wrong
Children should settle every adult disagreement
Children may explain a concern calmly and seek help when needed
Children should hide anything that worries them
questions.hint: Consider how listening and safety can go together.
questions.explanation: A child can be respectful and still speak honestly or ask a trusted adult for help.

questions.prompt: Name a way a cousin or grandparent can help a child learn respectful conduct. Give an example.
questions.hint: Think about what a child can learn by watching.
questions.explanation: A grandparent can model listening to each side of a disagreement, then invite the child to practise doing the same.

criteria.description: A grandparent can model listening to each side of a disagreement, then invite the child to practise doing the same.

questions.prompt: A sister apologises for speaking sharply. What could the other child do next to help them work together?
questions.hint: Think about both the hurt and the next conversation.
questions.explanation: They could acknowledge the apology, say calmly how they felt and agree on how to speak next time.

criteria.description: They could acknowledge the apology, say calmly how they felt and agree on how to speak next time.

questions.prompt: Which action helps relatives include a quieter child in planning a family activity?
options: Decide they are too quiet to contribute
Retell their idea before hearing it
Give every speaking turn to one relative
Ask for their idea and wait for an answer
questions.hint: Who has had time to speak?
questions.explanation: An invitation and time to answer help the quieter child contribute.

questions.prompt: Compare two responses to a mistake: laughing at a sibling and helping the sibling put it right. Which better promotes harmony, and why?
questions.hint: Trace how each response may affect the next task.
questions.explanation: Helping put it right supports repair and keeps the sibling involved. Laughing at the mistake can cause embarrassment or resentment.

criteria.description: Helping put it right supports repair and keeps the sibling involved. Laughing at the mistake can cause embarrassment or resentment.

questions.prompt: Plan a shared task for a child and an older relative. Allocate one action to each and explain how each can show respect.
questions.hint: Match each action to the person's ability.
questions.explanation: For tidying a table, the child can stack safe items and the adult can move a heavy object. Each can listen and thank the other.

criteria.description: For tidying a table, the child can stack safe items and the adult can move a heavy object. Each can listen and thank the other.

questions.prompt: An uncle changes a plan because an older relative needs help. What can a child do to support family harmony?
options: Ask which suitable part of the new plan they can help with
Refuse to listen because plans must never change
Decide the older relative is causing trouble
Promise to do work they cannot safely manage
questions.hint: Think about a safe, helpful response to a change.
questions.explanation: Asking about a suitable role shows care for others while keeping the task manageable.

questions.prompt: A learner says, “If two children disagree, one must have shown disrespect.” Give an example that challenges this claim.
questions.hint: Distinguish different ideas from hurtful conduct.
questions.explanation: Children may prefer different games yet listen, explain their choices and agree to take turns. Disagreement can be handled respectfully.

criteria.description: Children may prefer different games yet listen, explain their choices and agree to take turns. Disagreement can be handled respectfully.

questions.prompt: Explain to a younger pupil how listening, humility and keeping an agreement could help after an argument about chores.
questions.hint: Use the three actions in a sensible order.
questions.explanation: Listening reveals each person's concern. Admitting a mistake and keeping the new agreement can rebuild trust.

criteria.description: Listening reveals each person's concern. Admitting a mistake and keeping the new agreement can rebuild trust.

questions.prompt: A family meeting ends with a list of jobs, but one child feels unheard. Suggest two changes for the next meeting and explain how they support harmony.
questions.hint: Consider both how the meeting runs and how the duties are shared.
questions.explanation: Invite every child to speak before deciding and check that duties fit each person's ability. These changes support inclusion and cooperation.

criteria.description: Invite every child to speak before deciding and check that duties fit each person's ability. These changes support inclusion and cooperation.

indicators.content_standard: Discuss the need to obey and submit to authority

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 foundational, 7 simple-use, 5 application and 3 challenge questions.

indicators.statement: Explain the need for cordial relationships among family members.

questions.prompt: Which example best illustrates a cordial family relationship?
options: Two relatives discuss a problem kindly and make a shared plan
Two relatives avoid speaking about every problem
One relative insists on choosing for everyone
A family competes to see who deserves help
questions.hint: Cordial describes how people relate to each other.
questions.explanation: Friendly, respectful communication helps relatives work on a problem together.

questions.prompt: What word meaning friendly or warm completes “a _____ relationship”?
questions.hint: Look at the word used in this lesson's objective.
questions.explanation: A cordial relationship involves friendliness and goodwill.

questions.prompt: Why can listening carefully when a younger relative speaks help a family make a better plan?
questions.hint: Think about information that might be missed.
questions.explanation: The family may learn about a need that would otherwise be missed and adjust the plan to include that person.

criteria.description: The family may learn about a need that would otherwise be missed and adjust the plan to include that person.

questions.prompt: A relative shares news of a difficult week. Give an example of a caring response and explain one benefit.
questions.hint: Choose a response that leaves room for the person's wishes.
questions.explanation: One response is “Would it help if I sat with you?” Listening can help the relative feel supported.

criteria.description: One response is “Would it help if I sat with you?” Listening can help the relative feel supported.

questions.prompt: A family divides tasks to get a meal ready. What benefit of a cordial relationship does this illustrate?
options: Only the cook needs to know the plan
Cooperation can help the family meet a basic need
Food is provided simply by avoiding all discussion
A meal proves every family has equal resources
questions.hint: Consider the need being met and how the work is shared.
questions.explanation: Agreeing on tasks can help family members provide food together.

questions.prompt: Two siblings stop insulting each other and listen in turn. Explain how this change can support peace at home.
questions.hint: Follow the change from words to consequences.
questions.explanation: Taking turns allows both concerns to be heard. Removing insults makes it easier to settle the disagreement.

criteria.description: Taking turns allows both concerns to be heard. Removing insults makes it easier to settle the disagreement.

questions.prompt: Draw a simple chain from a respectful conversation to a family benefit. Label the steps.
questions.hint: Show the link between the conversation and the result.
questions.explanation: For example, conversation about a school need leads to a shared plan and then to someone helping get the needed item.

criteria.description: For example, conversation about a school need leads to a shared plan and then to someone helping get the needed item.

questions.prompt: What might a child learn by watching adults settle a disagreement fairly?
options: How to win by speaking over others
That all problems disappear without action
How to listen and make a fair agreement
That asking for another view wastes time
questions.hint: Think about learning through example.
questions.explanation: Adults can model habits that help a child develop considerate behaviour.

questions.prompt: Explain why a relative may be more willing to ask for help in a family where people speak kindly.
questions.hint: Think about how a past response affects the next request.
questions.explanation: Kind responses reduce the fear of being mocked. A relative may explain what they need sooner.

criteria.description: Kind responses reduce the fear of being mocked. A relative may explain what they need sooner.

questions.prompt: A cousin needs a quiet place to study. How could friendly discussion help a family support the cousin's progress?
questions.hint: Name a concrete change the family could agree on.
questions.explanation: Relatives could agree on a quiet time or a shared space, making study easier while considering other needs.

criteria.description: Relatives could agree on a quiet time or a shared space, making study easier while considering other needs.

questions.prompt: A learner says, “Cordial families must agree on every question.” Which example tests that idea?
options: Everyone stays silent during a discussion
One family member speaks on behalf of everyone
A disagreement is hidden from a younger child
Relatives prefer different plans and still speak with respect
questions.hint: Consider the difference between agreement and goodwill.
questions.explanation: People can disagree while listening, reasoning and continuing to care for each other.

questions.prompt: Make a two-column chart. Give one family behaviour in the first column and a benefit it can bring in the second. Add a different pair in the next row.
questions.hint: Connect each behaviour to a specific result.
questions.explanation: Listening can build understanding. Sharing suitable duties can help the household complete a task on time.

criteria.description: Listening can build understanding. Sharing suitable duties can help the household complete a task on time.

questions.prompt: How can an honest apology support a cordial relationship? Give one step that can follow the apology.
questions.hint: Consider what words and actions each contribute.
questions.explanation: An apology acknowledges harm. Repairing the mistake or changing the behaviour can help restore trust.

criteria.description: An apology acknowledges harm. Repairing the mistake or changing the behaviour can help restore trust.

questions.prompt: Why might relatives plan together when there is a cost for school materials?
options: They can discuss the need and decide what support is possible
A kind conversation automatically pays every expense
One child must find the whole amount alone
They can avoid finding out what is needed
questions.hint: Think about planning within the family's means.
questions.explanation: Cooperation helps relatives identify a need and organise available help.

questions.prompt: Show two brief ways to respond when a family duty is forgotten. Have an observer explain which response helps the family cooperate again.
questions.hint: Let the observer hear both replies.
questions.explanation: Compare blame with a calm reminder and a plan to finish the job. The observer can identify which response supports repair.

criteria.description: Compare blame with a calm reminder and a plan to finish the job. The observer can identify which response supports repair.

questions.prompt: A family works together to fix a torn window screen. Explain one link to family progress and one link to unity.
questions.hint: Separate what improved in the home from what improved between people.
questions.explanation: Completing the repair improves the home. Sharing the task and recognising each person's effort can strengthen unity.

criteria.description: Completing the repair improves the home. Sharing the task and recognising each person's effort can strengthen unity.

questions.prompt: Which observation gives the strongest evidence that a family's new listening routine is helping?
options: Everyone has stopped mentioning any difficulty
Relatives now raise concerns and agree on practical next steps
Only one person ever suggests a solution
The family wrote a rule but has never used it
questions.hint: Look for a change in what people do together.
questions.explanation: Being able to raise problems and make joint plans shows cooperation in action.

questions.prompt: Explain to a classmate why a family may still face material difficulties even when its relationships are cordial.
questions.hint: Distinguish cooperation from the resources available.
questions.explanation: Resources can be limited. Good relationships help relatives plan and support each other but cannot guarantee money or supplies.

criteria.description: Resources can be limited. Good relationships help relatives plan and support each other but cannot guarantee money or supplies.

questions.prompt: Compare peace based on listening with quiet caused by fear. Give one sign of each and explain which better supports family wellbeing.
questions.hint: Consider whether someone can speak honestly.
questions.explanation: Listening allows people to raise concerns and find agreement. Fear may silence concerns while problems remain, so genuine listening better supports wellbeing.

criteria.description: Listening allows people to raise concerns and find agreement. Fear may silence concerns while problems remain, so genuine listening better supports wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Write a short argument about why cordial relationships matter to a family. Use two different benefits and an example for each.
questions.hint: Use two distinct effects of the way people treat each other.
questions.explanation: For example, taking turns in a disagreement supports peace, while planning for a relative's school needs supports progress. Explain the connection in both cases.

criteria.description: For example, taking turns in a disagreement supports peace, while planning for a relative's school needs supports progress. Explain the connection in both cases.

indicators.statement: Identify attitudes and behaviours of a responsible family member.

questions.prompt: Which action shows responsibility at home?
questions.hint: Think about what the family has agreed and what a child can safely do.
questions.explanation: Finishing an agreed task helps the family rely on one another.
options: Claiming that a younger child should do all chores
Leaving an agreed duty without telling anyone
Taking credit for another relative's work

questions.prompt: Name one way to support a family member.
questions.hint: Think about what the relative needs and what you can safely do.
questions.explanation: Help respectfully, listen or share a suitable task

criteria.description: Help respectfully, listen or share a suitable task

questions.prompt: Two siblings want the same item. What is a fair response?
questions.hint: Consider both people's wishes.
questions.explanation: Take turns or seek a calm agreement

criteria.description: Take turns or seek a calm agreement

questions.prompt: Why is honest communication important in a family?
questions.hint: Think about what happens when people can rely on each other's words.
questions.explanation: Honesty makes it easier for family members to trust what they hear.

questions.prompt: What is one way to resolve a minor disagreement peacefully?
questions.hint: Choose a conversation that could repair the difficulty.
questions.explanation: Talk calmly and listen

criteria.description: Talk calmly and listen

questions.prompt: Explain why family members may have different responsibilities.
questions.hint: Think about what each person is able to do.
questions.explanation: Age, ability and roles differ

criteria.description: Age, ability and roles differ

questions.prompt: Which expectation is unfair?
questions.hint: Think about responsibilities appropriate for an adult and a child.
questions.explanation: Children can contribute at home while adults retain responsibility for adult problems.
options: A learner putting away their own books
A relative helping prepare a family meal
A child telling an adult when help is needed
A child solving every adult problem alone

questions.prompt: Match the action to the likely effect: sharing a task, apologising after a mistake, listening to a relative. Effects: showing respect, sharing effort, repairing trust.
questions.hint: Match the action to what it can do for a relationship.
questions.explanation: Sharing a task shares effort, apologising can help repair trust, and listening shows respect.

criteria.description: Sharing a task shares effort, apologising can help repair trust, and listening shows respect.

questions.prompt: A family member makes a mistake. What can help repair trust?
questions.hint: Consider both words and actions after a mistake.
questions.explanation: Honesty, apology and changed behaviour

criteria.description: Honesty, apology and changed behaviour

questions.prompt: How can a learner care for shared belongings?
questions.hint: Think about who uses the item next.
questions.explanation: Use them carefully and return/store them properly

criteria.description: Use them carefully and return/store them properly

questions.prompt: What should a child do when home feels unsafe?
questions.hint: Consider who can help keep a child safe.
questions.explanation: A trusted adult can help a child get support when something feels unsafe.
options: Tell a trusted adult who can help
Try to handle every danger alone
Assume asking for help is disloyal

questions.prompt: Draw family members cooperating on a safe task.
questions.hint: Give each person a suitable part of the activity.
questions.explanation: Clear cooperative activity

criteria.description: Clear cooperative activity

questions.prompt: Why is respect important between younger and older family members?
questions.hint: Consider the feelings of each person.
questions.explanation: It supports dignity and peaceful relationships

criteria.description: It supports dignity and peaceful relationships

questions.prompt: A caregiver is busy and asks for help with a safe task. What is a responsible response?
questions.hint: Think about the task, the learner's ability and asking for help.
questions.explanation: Help if able or explain respectfully

criteria.description: Help if able or explain respectfully

questions.prompt: Which action strengthens family trust?
questions.hint: Consider whether others can rely on the person's word.
questions.explanation: Keeping a reasonable promise shows other people that they can depend on you.
options: Agreeing to a duty you cannot do
Hiding a mistake to avoid discussion
Promising every relative the same item

questions.prompt: Role-play solving a household disagreement respectfully.
questions.hint: Show each person speaking and listening in turn.
questions.explanation: Listening, calm language and fair solution

criteria.description: Listening, calm language and fair solution

questions.prompt: Give one example of self-control at home.
questions.hint: Choose a way to pause before responding.
questions.explanation: Pause before anger, use words or walk away safely

criteria.description: Pause before anger, use words or walk away safely

questions.prompt: What does cooperation in a family support?
questions.hint: Think about how members share work while considering each other's needs.
questions.explanation: Cooperation helps families share work fairly and meet people's needs.
options: One person deciding all duties alone
An equal burden regardless of ability

questions.prompt: Describe one responsibility suitable for a learner and its benefit.
questions.hint: What can a younger relative safely do that helps someone else?
questions.explanation: A learner could keep a shared table clear before a meal so everyone has a clean place to eat. Accept another age-appropriate responsibility with a linked benefit.

criteria.description: A learner could keep a shared table clear before a meal so everyone has a clean place to eat. Accept another age-appropriate responsibility with a linked benefit.

questions.prompt: Why should family duties be shared fairly?
questions.hint: Consider different ages, needs and abilities.
questions.explanation: Different members can contribute according to age and ability

criteria.description: Different members can contribute according to age and ability
